corrections.name: Mohamed Elneny
corrections.evidence_summary: UEFA and LaLiga match records establish a competitive Arsenal appearance and goal against Dundalk on 10 December 2020, within 2020-21 to 2025-26. Fame 4 follows comparable established Arsenal midfielders.

corrections.name: Dietmar Hamann
corrections.evidence_summary: Manchester City explicitly describes his defensive-midfield role and competitive City seasons from 2006 to 2009, including his work at the midfield base in the 2007-08 Premier League campaign. The league profile independently identifies his City career. All precede 2025-26. Fame 4 reflects an established but less obvious veteran.

corrections.name: Mathew Ryan
corrections.evidence_summary: The federation match record names Mathew Ryan as Valencia starting goalkeeper in La Liga on 30 August 2015. Real Sociedad confirms goalkeeper identity and prior Valencia participation. Fame 3 follows comparable less prominent La Liga keepers.

corrections.name: Lautaro Javier Martínez
corrections.evidence_summary: Inter identifies Lautaro Martinez as an Argentine striker and documents his senior Argentina participation and established pre-cutoff career. Existing identity and fame preserved; needed playing-name aliases only.

corrections.name: Lautaro Martínez
corrections.evidence_summary: Inter documents his 100th and 101st Serie A goals on 25 February 2024. Short playing name identifies the existing accepted entry without changing fame or cutoff.

corrections.name: Bojan Krkić
corrections.evidence_summary: Barcelona official archive identifies Bojan and records 37 official first-team matches in 2010-11, within the required decade.

corrections.name: Kevin De Bruyne
corrections.evidence_summary: The Premier League documents his 100th assist on 8 April 2023 and uses KDB for the same player. This establishes both the threshold and alias before cutoff.

corrections.name: Rio Ferdinand
corrections.evidence_summary: United decade history identifies Rio Ferdinand in the 2002-03 title-winning team; UEFA contemporaneously records his competitive appearance against Leverkusen in November 2002. Add unique familiar first name only.

corrections.name: Xabier Alonso Olano
corrections.evidence_summary: Real Madrid maps full name to Xabi Alonso and records 236 competitive games during 2009-14; Liverpool records more than 200 club appearances before his 2009 move. Add familiar unique short name only.

corrections.name: Mohamed Salah
corrections.evidence_summary: Liverpool explicitly uses Mo Salah for Mohamed Salah and records his 2017 arrival, 44 goals in 2017-18 and 2019 Champions League final goal. Existing fame preserved.

corrections.name: Zlatan Ibrahimović
corrections.evidence_summary: Milan uses Ibra and Zlatan for the same player while recording 155 Serie A goals as of March 2023, already above threshold before cutoff.
